fixes.explanation: The text says Moses, Israel's leader, sprinkled the oil and the blood on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. “So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, as well as Aaron’s sons and their garments.” (Leviticus 8:30) The clothes are named right alongside the men. Garments shows up four times in that one verse, so it's hard to miss, baker.

The seventy elders aren't mentioned in this passage. Moses, Israel's leader, is told to “…assemble the whole congregation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” (Leviticus 8:3) That's not a handpicked group, friend. The word is whole.

Right, Moses, Israel's leader, asks for no extra days. The text says, “So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” (Leviticus 8:4) He does as he was commanded, and the assembly gathers. I'd have needed a reminder alarm and a sticky note.

Ashes don't show up in this washing. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…presented Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.” (Leviticus 8:6) Aaron, the one being ordained, and his sons are presented, and then the water comes. Water is the only thing the verse names.

Onyx stones don't appear anywhere in this passage, friend. I'd have guessed something sparkly too, because sprinkles are basically my whole personality. Moses, Israel's leader, sets “…the gold plate, the holy diadem, on the front of the turban…” (Leviticus 8:9) The front of the turban gets a gold plate.

Twelve is a big number, and I lose count at three when sprinkles are involved. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times…” (Leviticus 8:11) Seven is the number for the altar, friend.

The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.” (Leviticus 8:12) First the tabernacle and the altar get the oil. Then Aaron himself does, right on his head. It's the man too, not only the things.

The text says Moses, Israel's leader, brought the bull near for the sin offering “…and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.” (Leviticus 8:14) Hands, and on its head. Aaron and his sons are the ones doing it, baker.

The text doesn't say the people eat it. Moses, Israel's leader, “burned” the bull with its hide, flesh and dung “…outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded him.” (Leviticus 8:17) I'd have guessed a feast too, friend, because my brain goes to cookies at every gathering. The fat went on the altar, and the rest was burned outside the camp.

The crowd is gathered at the entrance, but the verse doesn't send any blood their way. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, slaughtered the ram “…and splattered the blood on all sides of the altar.” (Leviticus 8:19) The altar is the place the text names, and it says all sides.

The basin isn't named in this step, friend. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, “…washed the entrails and legs with water and burned the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering…” (Leviticus 8:21) Washed, then burned on the altar. Entire is the word to hold onto.

I'd have guessed bigger spots too, baker, but the text goes small. Moses, Israel's leader, put the blood “…on Aaron’s right earlobe, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.” (Leviticus 8:23) An earlobe, a thumb and a big toe, all on the right. Chest, shoulders and back aren't on the list.

The text says Moses, Israel's leader, put it all in the hands of Aaron and his sons “…and waved them before the LORD as a wave offering.” (Leviticus 8:27) The fat, the thigh and the bread are what's in their hands. Aaron and his sons are holding them when they're waved before the LORD. Nice work, baker.

They don't keep it. The text says Moses, Israel's leader, took these from their hands and “…burned them on the altar with the burnt offering.” (Leviticus 8:28) It's called “…an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.” So the answer is False, friend, because Aaron and his sons hand it over.

A doorpost is a sensible guess, friend, but the text puts the oil and blood on people and their clothes. Moses, Israel's leader, sprinkles them on Aaron and his sons “…and their garments.” (Leviticus 8:30) Everything lands on Aaron, his sons and what they're wearing.

Nothing gets saved for later, baker. Moses, Israel's leader, tells Aaron and his sons, “Then you must burn up the remainder of the meat and bread.” (Leviticus 8:32) First they boil the meat and eat it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting (Leviticus 8:31). Whatever remains goes into the fire.

Restitution sounds like a word that wears a tie, and I'd have picked it too, friend. But Moses, Israel's leader, says it was commanded by the LORD “…in order to make atonement on your behalf.” (Leviticus 8:34) The word he uses is atonement, and it's for Aaron and his sons.

Intercession is a fancy word, baker, and I'd have fallen for it too. But Moses, Israel's leader, tells Aaron and his sons it was commanded by the LORD “…in order to make atonement on your behalf.” (Leviticus 8:34) Atonement is what he says. And the words on your behalf are aimed right at Aaron and his sons.
